Remarks

A block is a very generic grouping of Tiles. This should be the root class for all derived blocks as it provides some basic implementations of the major interfaces of IEnumerable<T>, IBlock, IComparable<T>, and IEquatable<T>.

Constructors

Block(IEnumerable<Tile>)

Constructor. Optionally takes in an IEnumerable<T> of Tiles.

public Block(IEnumerable<Tile> tiles = null)

Parameters

tiles IEnumerable<Tile>

The Tiles that make up the block.

Remarks

In general, this (and the other constructors for derived classes) should not be used in favor of using IBlock static functions such as GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile>) or the GetPossibleBlockSets(IEnumerable<Tile>) static helper function.

Those methods will ensure that Blocks created correctly match their intended semantic meaning, such as Pungs having all the same tile or Chows having a sequence of tiles in the same suit.

Methods

CompareTo(Block)

Compares the current instance with another object of the same type and returns an integer that indicates whether the current instance precedes, follows, or occurs in the same position in the sort order as the other object.

public int CompareTo(Block that)

Parameters

that Block

A Block to compare with this instance.

Returns

int

A value that indicates the relative order of the objects being compared. The return value has these meanings:

ValueMeaning
Less than zeroThis instance precedes that in the sort order.
Zero This instance occurs in the same position in the sort order as that.
Greater than zeroThis instance follows that in the sort order.

Remarks

Comparison is done by comparing:

  1. if that is null (always 1)
  2. type (using GetHashCodeBasis())
  3. the number of tiles in the block
  4. the actual tiles in the block (after sorting) using CompareTo(Tile).

GetHashCode()

Serves as the default hash function.

public override int GetHashCode()

Returns

int

A hash code for the current object.

Remarks

Calculates hash value using the value returned from GetHashCodeBasis() as a basis which is then exponentiated using an exponent created using that same basis and the hash codes for the tiles of the block.

GetHashCodeBasis()

Get the hash code basis representing this block type, which will be exponentiated as a part of calculating GetHashCode().

public static int GetHashCodeBasis()

Returns

int

The basis to use when calculating hash codes for this block type.

Remarks

The number returned here should be a unique prime number among all derived Koffing.Blocks to ensure proper hashing. The current set of numbers is verified in GetBlockHashCodeIsCorrect(Block, int).

GetPossibleHelper(IEnumerable<Tile>, Type)

Protected static helper function that can be used to simplify overrides of GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile>).

protected static IEnumerable<MadeBlockContext> GetPossibleHelper(IEnumerable<Tile> tiles, Type blockType)

Parameters

tiles IEnumerable<Tile>

Examples

As an example of such an override taken from GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile>):

public static new IEnumerable<MadeBlockContext> GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile> tiles)
{
	return GetPossibleHelper(tiles, typeof(Chow)).Distinct();
}

Note that the call to Distinct<TSource>(IEnumerable<TSource>) is necessary, as this function does not do it itself.

Remarks

Most derived blocks have their logic for the GetPossible(IEnumerable<Tile>) function implemented as an override of GetPossibleForTile(Tile, IEnumerable<Tile>), as it is often easier to write logic around a single given tile. Rather than duplicating the logic to go through all distinct tiles and calling GetPossibleForTile(Tile, IEnumerable<Tile>) for each one, this function can be used instead.
